..
Issued at 1217 PM CDT Fri Aug 28 2026

Today and Tonight...

Water vapor imagery and objective analysis late this morning depict 
mid-level ridging centered over the Desert Southwest and Permian 
Basin with subsequent troughing in place over the northeastern 
CONUS. Lingering cloud cover from morning showers has broken up, 
allowing for plenty of sunshine and high temperatures in the mid to 
upper 80s today. 

A shortwave disturbance pushing from the front range into the 
northern Plains will spin up a surface low that will track eastward 
across SD and into MN into the weekend. As a result, a tightening 
surface pressure gradient and strengthening LLJ, combined with 
increasing afternoon mixing, will lead to stronger southerly winds 
gusts through the day. Gusts will peak in the 20-30 mph range across 
much of the area, with gust up to 35 mph possible across northeast 
Nebraska. Although mixing will taper off after the sun goes down, 
the tightening surface pressure gradient will keep 20-30 mph wind 
gusts in place overnight. 

The aforementioned shortwave disturbance and associated surface low 
will initiate a round of thunderstorms across southeast SD 
overnight, with a trailing line of showers and thunderstorms 
expected to push southward across the area overnight into Saturday 
morning. Shower and thunderstorm coverage will become more broken 
with southward extent as large scale forcing for ascent decreases, 
bringing PoPs of 15-30% in place into early Saturday. While severe 
weather is not expected due to the limited instability, showers may 
help to bring the gusty winds aloft to the surface, with localized 
gusts in the 40-45 mph range possible. 

Saturday and Sunday... 

Temperatures will trend warmer through this weekend as the 
aforementioned mid-level ridge pulls eastward into the central and 
southern Plains and lee troughing strengthens over the northern 
Plains. Lingering showers and cloud cover into late Saturday morning 
will bring lower confidence in high temperatures. High temperatures 
are expected in the low to mid 90s, with the upper 90s possible if 
cloud cover clears quicker than expected. South-southwesterly wind 
gusts of 20-30 mph will continue through Saturday, helping to pull 
low-level moisture advection into the area and push dewpoints into 
the upper 60s. As a result, heat index values are expected to peak 
in the upper 90s, with a few spots hitting 100. 

Sunday looks to be the warmest day of the period for most locations, 
with plenty of sunshine and persistent ridging pushing high 
temperatures into the upper 90s. Heat Index values are expected in 
the 99 to 103 degree range, just shy of Heat Advisory criteria at 
the moment. A shortwave trough rounding the ridge and pushing across 
the northern Plains will force a trailing cold front southward 
across Nebraska through Sunday, likely waiting until later Sunday or 
early Monday to reach eastern Nebraska. Ahead of this boundary, a 
modestly unstable, yet capped, air mass is expected to develop. 
Sufficient instability and deep layer shear along with steepening 
lapse rates will bring the potential for strong to severe storms, 
conditional on if convective inhibition can be overcome. Given the 
lower confidence in initiation, PoPs currently peak at 15-20% Sunday 
night into early Monday. SPC has placed much of eastern Nebraska in 
a Marginal Risk (Level 1 of 5) for severe weather.

Monday and Beyond... 

Into the work week, the ridge will gradually shift east into the mid-
South and dampen as shortwave disturbances track over the top of the 
ridge. As a result, southwesterly to zonal flow will return aloft 
and temperatures will ease slightly, though still remain slightly 
above seasonal averages. High temperatures are expected in the upper 
80s to low 90s through the work week. Additionally, the dampened 
ridge will leave the area vulnerable to passing shortwave 
disturbance, bringing periodic precipitation chances (15-30%) 
through the week. Confidence in the timing and extent of these 
precipitation chances remains tied to subtle wave timing and 
mesoscale details, which should become clearer with time.
